title: Tamil Union enters quarter-finals with sixth straight win | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:20
-     - 9

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Tamil Union captained by Navod Paranavithana stamped their authority in the Major Club T20 tournament securing their sixth win out of six to finish on top of Group A and thus qualify for a place in the quarter-finals.

At the receiving end at SSC grounds yesterday was BRC who were beaten by nine wickets. The highlight of the match was the scorching century scored by Thanuka Dabare as Tamil Union chased down BRC’s moderate total of 133-7 to win with 35 balls to spare. Dabare spanked 2 fours and 11 sixes mounting a devastating attack on the hapless BRC bowlers as he raced to his unbeaten century off 50 balls. BRC’s batting was derailed by the right-arm seam of Lahiru Samarakoon who turned up with figures of 4/23. Dulaj Ashen was the only batsman to withstand Samarakoon’s seam movement scoring 48 off 49 balls.

Moors SC and CCC also kept their chances alive of qualifying for a place in the last four with victories. Moors SC thumped Nugegoda SWC by seven wickets at the P Sara Oval with skipper Pasindu Sooriyabandara (59 off 34 balls, 7 fours, 2 sixes) and Sohan de Livera (64 off 42 balls, 7 fours, 1 six) setting the stage for the win with an opening stand of 120 off 69 balls. Wiry right-arm fast bowler Garuka Sanketh (4/31) rattled through the Nugegoda SWC batting restricting them to 157-8 where Pulindu Perera made the only noteworthy contribution with 71 off 44 balls (11 fours, 1 six).

Former Nalandian Chamindu Wijesinghe produced a fine all-round performance (42 off 18 balls, 5 sixes and 3/20) to star in CCC’s 103-run win against Police SC at the NCC grounds. Kamindu Mendis (71 off 43 balls, 5 fours, 5 sixes) top scored in CCC’s total of 197-7. Police SC were shot out for 94 with Test star Sonal Dinusha taking 2/5 off his 4 overs.

SSC also secured a place in the quarter-finals with their fourth win in five matches to consolidate their position at the top of Group B. In a low scoring game played at the NCC grounds, Panadura SC were dismissed for 128 with left-arm seamer Mihiranga Silva taking 3/22 supported by national cricketers Prabath Jayasuriya, Kasun Rajitha and Dunith Wellalage with two wickets apiece. SSC romped home by seven wickets mounting their run chase on the third wicket pair skipper Avishka Fernando (66 off 43 balls, 4 fours, 4 sixes) and Nuwanidu Fernando (48* off 39 balls, 4 fours, 2 sixes) who put on 114 off 13 overs after SSC lost their first two wickets for four runs in the first over.

NCC moved to second place behind SSC with a five-wicket win against Ace Capital CC at the P Sara Oval. Excellent bowling by pacie Chamika Gunasekara (4/21) tied Ace Capital CC down to 117-8. Off-spinner Traveen Mathew (3/32) rattled the NCC top order reducing them to 35-4 before Lahiru Udara (47 off 34 balls, 4 fours, 2 sixes) with the help of Kavin Bandara and Chamika Karunaratne saw NCC home with 21 balls to spare.

Bloomfield beat Colts by four wickets at the SSC grounds with both teams out of contention for a quarter-final place. Colts scored 114-9 and Bloomfield replied with 119-6. Sanuka Galagoda top scored with 56* (off 43 balls, 7 fours, 2 sixes).

title: Shehara (6/25) bowls Badureliya CC to victory | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:05
-     - 8

Badureliya CC captain Sumudu Nisansala with the Gwen Herat memorial trophy and cash award

Eighteen-year-old Shehara Induwari from Devapathiraja College, Rathgama produced a deadly spell of off-spin bowling taking 6/25 off 10 overs to bowl Badureliya CC to a comprehensive 97 runs win over Panadura SC in the Major Club Women’s limited-over final played at the Colts grounds yesterday.

Panadura SC were bundled out for 105 after losing their first five wickets for 15 runs chasing a target of 203. A 50-run stand for the sixth wicket between Amadhi Wijesinghe (21) and Rashmika Sewwandi (48 off 73 balls, 6 fours) saw them cross the 100-run mark. Badureliya CC invited to bat first put up a decent total of 202-7 with skipper Sumudu Nisansala (56 off 105 balls, 4 fours) and Rashmi Nethranjali (30) putting together a partnership of 90 for the fourth wicket. Seamer Piumi Wathsala captured 4/27 for Panadura SC.

Shehara took the Player of the Final award of Rs. 75,000 as well as the Best Bowler of the Tournament award of Rs. 100,000, while her team Badureliya CC collected a cheque for Rs. 500,000 and the Gwen Herath memorial trophy as champions. Panadura SC received Rs. 300,000 as runner-up. The Best Batter of the Tournament award of Rs. 100,000 was won by Nilakshika Silva (who is currently away in Dubai for the Women’s Asia Cup), and the Most Valuable Player award of Rs. 150,000 was won by Malki Madara. The awards were presented by SLC Head of National Cricket Operations Chinthaka Edirimanne and Shamara Herat, daughter of late Mrs. Gwen Herat. (ST)

Scores: 

Badureliya CC 202-7 (50) (Nethagi Isuranjali 22, Sumudu Nisansala 56, Rashmi Nethranjali 30, Sachini Nisansala 21, Piumi Wathsala 4/27, Devagi Jeganathan 2/31) beat Panadura SC 105 (33.4) (Amadhi Wijesinghe 21, Rashmika Sewwandi 48, Shehara Induwari 6/25)

title: Messi retires from international football | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:04
-     - 8

Argentina great Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football, saying it was a decision that “hurt” but “the time has come”.

The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances, making him the country’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

In a statement, Messi said he has given everything to the national side but now has “nothing left to give”. He added: “Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply.

“I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team.

“I’ve given it my all, I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some really great young players coming through behind me who deserve their chance.”

His career will continue at club level with Major League Soccer team Inter Miami, where he has a contract that runs to the end of the 2028 season.

title: A newspaper gown and an NBA tribute - Osaka’s US Open fashion statement | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:03
-     - 7

The spectacular jellyfish outfit at the Australian Open. A sparkly Eiffel Tower-inspired golden dress at the French Open. The elegant all-white Japanese kimono at Wimbledon.

Naomi Osaka has proved she knows how to make a grand entrance at the Grand Slams - and her arrival at this year’s US Open was always going to turn more heads.

The four-time major champion was draped in a hooded white gown - with cuttings of newspaper headlines about her career highlights sewn in - when she walked out for her first-round match against Russia’s Anastasia Zakharova in New York.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played as she fought her way to a 7-6 (8-6) 7-6 (7-3) win over world number 101 Zakharova.

Afterwards Osaka said the on-court look was inspired by NBA legend Allen Iverson, who is widely credited for introducing a sharper focus on fashion in his sport during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Osaka’s performance on the court in Monday’s night session was less stylish, however.

The Japanese 13th seed, who won the Flushing Meadows title in 2018 and 2020, faltered after a strong start and ultimately needed to dig deep to see off Zakharova.

title: Former Sri Lanka fast bowler Keerthi Gunaratne dies at 71 | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:02
-     - 11

Keerthi Gunaratne

Sri Lanka lost one of its most dedicated cricketers and Coach Keerthi Gunaratne who played for his country in the pre-Test era.

Gunaratne who died at the age of 71 was a right-arm medium-fast bowler who figured prominently in domestic cricket playing for Saracens SC in division I cricket for several years. He represented Sri Lanka teams in the early eighties before the country gained Test status.

Following his playing career Gunaratne turned to cricket coaching where he gained high recognition coaching school teams like his alma mater St. Peter’s College, Colombo, Nalanda College and Wesley College across different eras. 

Sri Lanka Cricket appointed him as the District Coach for Jaffna. He is widely credited with selflessly sacrificing years to develop, mentor, and shape the cricket infrastructure and young talents in the North. He was heavily celebrated within the local sporting community for his contributions to schools, regional districts, and club-level cricket.

Gunaratne acted as a mentor to national players like Dhammika Prasad, who publicly credited him for fundamentally building and guiding his international cricket career.

Prasad posted on social media: “I lost someone who was much more than a coach to me. Keerthi Gunaratne, a former Ceylon cricketer, my loving coach, my mentor, my inspiration, and, above all, my second father.”

Gunaratne began his education at De La Salle College (Mutuwal) before moving to St. Peter’s College. Apart from cricket, he was a versatile athlete who represented his school at rugby. (ST)

title: United Southern, Leo CC, Army, Negombo enter semi-finals | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 2 September 2026 00:00
-     - 8

The quarter-final matches of the Tier B T20 tournament played out at four venues saw United Southern SC, Leo CC, Army SC and Negombo CC enter the semif-finals.

Leo CC completed the most comprehensive win of the four matches beating Navy SC by 98 runs at Air Force grounds, Katunayake. Two half-century stands for the first two wickets involving Ashan Fernando (54 off 35 balls, 6 fours, 2 sixes) – 59 off 37 balls with Prasad Asanka (40 off 27 balls, 7 fours, 1 six) and 50 off 36 balls with Nethma Karunaratne (18) saw Leo CC reach 174-6 off their allotted overs. Navy SC were shot out for 76 inside 15 overs mainly by Supun Dilshan (3/17).

Amy SC went through some anxious moments before beating Moratuwa SC by 14 runs at Welisara. Despite being reduced to 97-7 chasing 190, Moratuwa SC put up a plucky performance through their late order and tail to reply with 175-9. Madushanka Premaratne staged a recovery with a brilliant half-century (51 off 23 balls, 5 fours, 4 sixes) falling in the final over. Janaka Sampath top scored for Army SC with an aggressive 61 off 47 balls (4 fours, 2 sixes) in their total of 189-7.

Both Negombo CC and United Southern SC defended their low totals to beat Ragama CC and Sebastianites respectively. Negombo CC scored 139-7 and dismissed Ragama CC for 91 to win by 48 runs at Air Force grounds, Katunayake, while United Southern SC scored 143-8 and bowled out Sebastianites for 98 at Welisara. Damesh Mathishan top scored with 60 (off 46 balls, 3 fours, 3 sixes) and left-arm seamer Lidula Nuwanga took 4/20 for United Southern SC.

In the semi-finals scheduled for 4 September Leo CC will play United Southern SC in the first semi-final and Army SC take on Negombo CC in the second semi-final. (ST)
